articles.title: Bay Depression: IMD Warns of Heavy Rain in Coastal AP - Deccan Chronicle

articles.full_text:
District administrations along the coastal belt have been placed on alert to manage civic inundation, monitor reservoir levels, and initiate relief measures where necessary.
Visakhapatnam: Heavy rainfall is likely at isolated places over coastal AP and Yanam on Tuesday. Strong winds are also predicted in several areas.
Stating this, an IMD report said on Monday that the well-marked low pressure area over east central and adjoining west central Bay of Bengal moved west north westwards and lay over west central and adjoining east central Bay of Bengal on Monday.
The associated cyclonic circulation extended upto 7.6km above mean sea level. “This is very likely to move west-northwestwards and intensify into a depression over west central Bay of Bengal during next 24 hours and into a deep depression over west central and adjoining northwest Bay of Bengal during the subsequent 24 hours,” the report issued in the evening said.
Continuing to move west-northwestwards, this is very likely to reach near north Andhra Pradesh - South Odisha coasts around morning of September 23.
Under its influence, heavy to very heavy rain is likely at isolated places over coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam on Tuesday.
Thunderstorms accompanied with lightning likely at isolated places coastal Andhra Pradesh, Yanam and Rayalaseema. Gusty winds speed reaching 40-50 kmph likely at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam.
Strong winds speed reaching 40-50 Kmph likely at isolated places over Rayalaseema.
On September 23 and 24, heavy to very heavy rain with extremely heavy falls is likely at isolated places over Coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam. Thunderstorms accompanied with lightning are likely at isolated places in coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam and Rayalaseema.
Squally winds speed reaching 50-60 Kmph are likely at isolated places over coastal Andhra Pradesh and Yanam . Strong wind-speed reaching 30-40 Kmph is likely at isolated places over Rayalaseema.
The same weather conditions will prevail on September 25 also, the IMD said.
Private weather forecasting agency Skymet said the weather system does have the potential to shape itself into a cyclone before crossing the coast. More would be known after the system becomes a depression over the west-central Bay of Bengal.
